reasons: The cited text (§ 7.6) imposes USD 25,000/day liquidated damages payable by Customer, which squarely triggers rule LD and is correctly classified as a high-severity deviation.

The redline reaches the preferred position by removing the Customer-payable LD entirely and expressly stating Customer has no liability for liquidated damages, penalties or other pre-agreed amounts for dependency delays.

The substituted remedy (Vendor excused only to the extent and for so long as the delay prevents performance, plus equitable schedule adjustment) is a proportionate, standard trade that preserves Vendor's legitimate delay interest without creating new Customer payment exposure or open-ended relief.

The high changed-character ratio is justified: the clause is a single sentence whose sole operative content is the prohibited LD, so deletion plus a neutral replacement necessarily rewrites it; no smaller edit would remove the penalty.
The comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and in the required voice; it states what changed and cites the playbook position without lecturing.
